raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A decode allocation sometimes needs only a few pages but evicts a much longer FULL radix leaf. Keeping the reusable prefix can reduce KV eviction on the next turn.

## Modifications

Add the opt-in `SGLANG_PYTHON_RADIX_EVICT_TAIL_CHUNK_SIZE` to the Python unified radix tree. The default is zero. On an eligible device-only FULL leaf, split a page-aligned suffix sufficient for the allocator’s shortfall, preserve prefix recency, and let the normal eviction walk reclaim the suffix. The option is documented in the environment reference.

## Accuracy Tests

The measured feature commit was `4702f1d847cc`. The submission head `0fe6e0d1df4f` merges the fixed upstream `40a64e1b5ba0`. Its complete Git tree was verified to equal applying the measured PR patch to that upstream commit.

The radix-tree, allocation-eviction and decode-lock suites passed **30 tests** on Linux arm64 CPU. They cover retained cache slots, locked prefixes, reuse after eviction, fallbacks and argument validation. The native A2 allocator test verified device contents after the evicted slots were overwritten.

```sh
python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_full_leaf_tail_eviction.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_allocation_eviction.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py
```

The four-host PD handoff returned 323 and 324 on a two-turn arithmetic smoke test. A broad model-quality suite was not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

On two 910B4 hosts, a full allocator with a 32,768-token leaf and a 1,280-token shortfall freed **32,768 → 4,096** tokens with the option set to 4,096, retaining **28,672** tokens for the next turn. At an 8,192-token shortfall it freed 8,192, and at a 32,768-token shortfall it freed the whole leaf. [Allocator reproducer and byte checks](https://github.com/INBreezefall/sglang/tree/682f1c33931c4b8c0ab11df9d0236d00ff06fcfb/benchmark/ascend_a2_pd_evidence).

In the full replay the two controls evicted **6,367,104 / 6,282,112** D tokens and the two PR runs evicted **4,525,824 / 5,311,232**, a mean reduction of **22.2%**. Mean TTFT was **15.5% lower**. Both P95 TTFTs were higher, both output rates were lower, and both native D decode rates fell inside the control range.

GLM-5.2 W4A8C8 ran on four hosts with eight Ascend 910B4-1 NPUs each, CANN 9.1.0 and torch-npu 2.10.0.post6. P and D each used TP16 and attention DP8. Every arm used SGLang `40a64e1b5ba0` with the same A2 C8 / Mooncake compatibility fixes. Each row contains all 72 responses from the same 24 sessions × three closed-loop turns, after 24 warm-ups. Temperature was 0, output was capped at 256 tokens, and retries were disabled.

| Arm | Mean TTFT (s) | P95 TTFT (s) | Client decode (tok/s per request, valid n/72) | D decode (tok/s) | Output TPS (tok/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Control 1 | 296.74 | 620.25 | 94.71 (53) | 36.41 | 9.47 |
| Restored control | 272.47 | 580.21 | 119.61 (57) | 45.99 | 9.31 |
| PR run 1 | 241.30 | 710.53 | 87.57 (57) | 38.67 | 8.96 |
| PR run 2 | 239.67 | 741.02 | 93.67 (51) | 45.25 | 9.28 |

Client decode averages valid semantic streaming spans. The PD relay can buffer output. D decode is the inverse of token-weighted server ITL, covering every post-first token interval. Output TPS counts actual output tokens over the formal wall window. The complete comparison allowed 1,200 s for the first token and 300 s between subsequent events. A separate original 300 s control completed 38 of 50 attempted requests before its stop policy withheld 22. [Protocol and anonymized per-request results](https://github.com/INBreezefall/sglang/tree/26bc7bdac9a4158319a7d3d8e3cd10218072bb05/benchmark/ascend_a2_pd_evidence/c24).

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted the changed Python files and ran scoped Ruff/isort checks.
- [x] Added or updated registered unit tests for the changed paths.
- [x] Updated the relevant option documentation.
- [x] Reported correctness checks, repeated hardware measurements, and regressions.
- [x] Checked the changed files against the project code-style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

Requesting codeowner review and the required upstream CI runs. Please merge once the required approvals and checks pass. files.patch: @@ -1444,6 +1444,11 @@ SGLang supports various environment variables that can be used to configure its Multiplier applied to the sliding-window-attention eviction interval. 1.0 + + SGLANG_PYTHON_RADIX_EVICT_TAIL_CHUNK_SIZE + Minimum number of tokens to free from a selected long leaf in the Python unified radix tree. A positive multiple of the page size enables partial eviction for plain, unsharded, device-only FULL caches without session references. The default evicts the whole leaf. + 0 + SGLANG_RADIX_FORCE_MISS Force radix-cache misses (debugging/benchmarking).

@@ -787,6 +787,9 @@ class Envs:
     # - Source builds with a missing or unusable Rust toolchain.
     # This also applies when Rust is explicitly selected.
     SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND = EnvStr("rust")
+    # Minimum tail to free when splitting an oversized device-only FULL leaf.
+    # Python TreeCore only. Zero keeps whole-leaf eviction.
+    SGLANG_PYTHON_RADIX_EVICT_TAIL_CHUNK_SIZE = EnvInt(0)
     # Once decode passes the sliding window, drop the SWA part of the prefill's
     # tree lock; its SWA KV becomes evictable rather than freed.
     SGLANG_OPT_RELEASE_PREFILL_SWA = EnvBoolWithAlias(

@@ -245,6 +245,42 @@ def _evict_device_end(self) -> None:
         self._evict_device_heap = []
         self._evict_device_last_node = None
 
+    def trim_eviction_leaf(
+        self, node_id: NodeId, remaining: int, *, chunk: int
+    ) -> None:
+        """Keep a reusable prefix. The selected node ID still denotes the suffix."""
+        core = self.tree_core
+        if (
+            core.enable_hicache
+            or core.enable_storage
+            or core.enable_external_cache_linker
+            or core.is_host_memory_buffer_only
+        ):
+            return
+        node = core.node_by_id(node_id)
+        data = node.component_data[self.component_type]
+        if (
+            remaining <= 0
+            or node.children
+            or node.backuped
+            or data.value is None
+            or data.lock_ref
+            or data.host_lock_ref
+            or data.session_ref
+            or node.write_through_pending_id is not None
+            or node.load_back_pending_id is not None
+        ):
+            return
+        release = (remaining + chunk - 1) // chunk * chunk
+        keep = len(node.key) - release
+        if keep < chunk:
+            return
+        last_access = node.last_access_time
+        parent, action = core._split_node(node.key, node, keep)
+        assert action is None
+        # Splitting for eviction does not constitute an access to the prefix.
+        parent.last_access_time = node.last_access_time = last_access
+
     def drive_host_eviction(
         self,
         num_tokens: int,

+import unittest
+from array import array
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.base_prefix_cache import EvictParams, InsertParams
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixKey
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.kits.unified_radix_cache.config import CacheConfig
+from sglang.test.kits.unified_radix_cache.fixtures import build_fixture, match_prefix
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=3, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestFullLeafTailEviction(unittest.TestCase):
+    def make_cache(self, chunk=8, *, session_cache=False):
+        with (
+            envs.SGLANG_PYTHON_RADIX_EVICT_TAIL_CHUNK_SIZE.override(chunk),
+            patch(
+                "sglang.test.kits.unified_radix_cache.fixtures.get_device",
+                return_value="cpu",
+            ),
+        ):
+            return build_fixture(
+                CacheConfig(page_size=4, kv_size=64, num_layers=1),
+                tree_core_backend="python",
+                enable_session_radix_cache=session_cache,
+            )[:2]
+
+    def insert(self, cache, allocator, tokens):
+        indices = allocator.alloc(len(tokens))
+        self.assertIsNotNone(indices)
+        cache.insert(InsertParams(key=RadixKey(array("q", tokens)), value=indices))
+        return indices
+
+    def assert_prefix(self, cache, tokens, expected):
+        match = match_prefix(cache, tokens)
+        self.assertEqual(match.device_prefix_len, len(expected))
+        actual = cache.tree_core.collect_full_device_indices(
+            match.last_device_node, cache.root_node_handle()
+        )
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, expected))
+
+    def test_allocation_shortfall_preserves_prefix_and_returns_slots_once(self):
+        cache, allocator = self.make_cache()
+        tokens = list(range(32))
+        indices = self.insert(cache, allocator, tokens)
+        free_before = allocator.available_size()
+        result = cache.evict_for_alloc(EvictParams(num_tokens=5))
+        self.assertEqual(result.num_tokens_evicted, 8)
+        self.assertEqual(allocator.available_size(), free_before + 8)
+        self.assert_prefix(cache, tokens, indices[:24])
+        cache.sanity_check()
+        result = cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=24))
+        self.assertEqual(result.num_tokens_evicted, 24)
+        self.assertEqual(allocator.available_size(), free_before + 32)
+        reused = allocator.alloc(allocator.available_size())
+        self.assertEqual(reused.unique().numel(), reused.numel())
+
+    def test_locked_prefix_survives_and_short_suffix_is_evicted_whole(self):
+        cache, allocator = self.make_cache()
+        tokens = list(range(32))
+        indices = self.insert(cache, allocator, tokens)
+        prefix = match_prefix(cache, tokens[:12]).last_device_node
+        lock = cache.inc_lock_ref(prefix).to_dec_params()
+        try:
+            self.assertEqual(
+                cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=8)).num_tokens_evicted, 8
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(
+                cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=8)).num_tokens_evicted, 12
+            )
+            self.assert_prefix(cache, tokens, indices[:12])
+            self.assertEqual(
+                cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=1)).num_tokens_evicted, 0
+            )
+            cache.sanity_check()
+        finally:
+            cache.dec_lock_ref(prefix, lock)
+
+    def test_default_and_session_cache_keep_whole_leaf_eviction(self):
+        for chunk, sessions in ((0, False), (8, True)):
+            with self.subTest(chunk=chunk, sessions=sessions):
+                cache, allocator = self.make_cache(chunk, session_cache=sessions)
+                self.insert(cache, allocator, list(range(32)))
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    cache.evict(EvictParams(num_tokens=5)).num_tokens_evicted, 32
+                )
+
+    def test_invalid_chunk_size(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "page multiple"):
+            self.make_cache(6)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
